classification: Six reviewed actual-matrix spectral rounding, complementarity and scalar-relaxation results; original convergence OPEN
conclusions: Cross singular-moment rounding has an exact quartic error and a cap-free clipped variant.
Original positive/negative spectral phases yield cubic and nuclear constraints; the bootstrap has original norm error O_C(n^(5/4)) under only Phi(A)<=C n^(3/2).
Every optimal diagonal SDP is block-balanced; zero canonical gap is equivalent to equal nonzero singular values and forces a scalar optimum, not conversely.

Canonical negative sign mass is at most half its actual SDP gap, or one quarter for a scalar optimal dual. Tensor mixing gives a strictly stronger necessary limiting curve below beta/tau=2/pi, with cap-free O_(C,t)(n^(5/4)) error for fixed t.
The evaluated scalar diagnostic bounds repair trace without a source operator cap. At the old strongest-feedback endpoint, repaired positivity gives normalized squared upper below 9/20.

Weak feedback admits a formal Dirac moment law satisfying the entire mixed family and exact fourth-moment refinement, yet the fully metric-optimized retained two-trace/Jensen bound has a uniform positive gap above target. This is moment-relaxation insufficiency, not an actual-width lower bound.
not_proved: Realization of the formal moment law by an actual complete signing, scalar optimal Gram, or compatible source and joint shell.
Scalar optimality or favorable source/cross alignment for every optimizer.
Original all-orders convergence or any identified limit value.

published_theorem_scope.statement_used: The real Grothendieck constant is strictly below pi/(2 asinh(1)) by a uniform positive effective margin.
published_theorem_scope.scope: Primary theorem statement directly checked; the full published proof was not independently reviewed here. The literal old Krivine endpoint is excluded for actual matrices. The retained-moment diagnostic does not impose every published constraint.

next_target: Actual optimal-Gram/coordinate and source-cross compatibility at admissible nearby ratios or a uniform range; not realization of the published-theorem-excluded exact old endpoint or re-optimization of the insufficient moment-only functional.
